When He, glorified is He, finished mentioning the state of the disbelievers and comparing their trial to the trial of the people of the garden mentioned, He mentioned the state of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) and the good He has prepared for them.

He said: (p-١٥٢٠)﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing with their Lord are gardens of bliss.﴾ That is: for the God-fearing, who avoid what brings down His wrath, of disbelief and sins, with Him, mighty and majestic, in the Hereafter, are gardens of pure bliss, which is not mixed with turbidity and not spoiled by fear of its ending.

﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals?﴾ The interrogative is for denial (istinkar).

The chieftains of the disbelievers of Quraysh used to see their great share in this world and the small shares of the Muslims in it. When they heard the mention of the Hereafter and what Allah gives the Muslims in it, they said: "If what Muhammad claims is true, our state and theirs will be nothing but like their state in this world." So Allah, refuting them and rejecting their claim, said: ﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims...﴾ and the verse. The fa' here is for coordination (ataf) upon an implied clause, like its counterparts.

Then Allah rebuked them and said: ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ This crooked judgment, as if the matter of recompense were entrusted to you, so that you judge about it as you wish.

﴿Or do you have a scripture in which you study?﴾ That is: in which you read, and so you find the obedient equal to the disobedient. Similar to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do you have a clear authority? So bring your scripture.﴾ [al-Saffat: 156-157]. Then He, glorified is He, said: "Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose." The majority (al-Jumhur) read inna with a kasra, taking it as governed by tadrusun, meaning: you study in the Book.

﴿Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose.﴾ When the lam entered, the hamza was given a kasra, as in His saying: "I knew that you are indeed intelligent," with a kasra. Or it is by way of hikaya (quoting) of what is studied, as in His saying: ﴿And We left upon him among the later generations﴾ ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds﴾ [al-Saffat: 78-79]. It was said: the speech is complete at His saying: "you study," then He began: ﴿Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose﴾, meaning: it is not for you to have that. Talhah ibn Musarrif and al-Dahhak read anna lakum with a fath on the hamza, taking the governing element to be tadrusun together with the addition of the emphatic lam. The meaning of takhayyarun is: you choose and desire.

Then He, glorified is He, increased the rebuke, and said: ﴿Or do you have oaths binding upon Us, extending to the Day of Resurrection?﴾ That is: firm, confirmed, utterly conclusive covenants. The meaning: Or do you have oaths upon Allah by which you secured that He would admit you into the Garden? His saying ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾ is connected to the implied element in lakum, meaning: they are established for you until the Day of Resurrection, and We are not released from their obligation until He judges you on that day. The answer to the oath is His saying: ﴿Indeed, for you is what you judge,﴾ because the meaning of ﴿Or do you have oaths﴾ is: or have We sworn to you?

Al-Razi said: The meaning is: Or have We guaranteed to you and sworn to you with emphatic oaths, utterly conclusive in affirmation?

It was also said: the speech is complete at His saying: ﴿to the Day of Resurrection,﴾ then He began: ﴿Indeed, for you is what you judge,﴾ meaning: the matter is not so.

The majority read bali'ah with a raf', as an attribute of aymān. al-Hasan and Zayd ibn Ali read it with a nasb, as a state (hal) of aymān, since it has been specified by the attribute, or of the pronoun in lakum, or of the pronoun in ʿalayna.

﴿Ask them, which of them stands surety for that?﴾ That is: ask them, O Muhammad, rebuking and reproaching them: which of them guarantees that judgment, which departs from what is right, that they will have in the Hereafter what the Muslims have there?

Ibn Kaysan said: al-Za'im here means the one who upholds the argument and the claim.

al-Hasan said: al-Za'im is the Messenger.

﴿Or do they have partners?﴾ who share with them in this statement, agreeing with them upon it. ﴿Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful﴾ in what they say. This is a command of incapacitation (taʿjiz), and the answer of the condition is omitted. It was also said: the meaning is: or do they have partners whom they make equal to the Muslims in the Hereafter?

﴿On the Day when the shin is uncovered﴾ "Yawm" is a time-adverb for His saying "let them bring," meaning: let them bring them on the Day when the shin is uncovered. It may also be an adverb governed by an implied verb, meaning: remember the Day when it is uncovered.

al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said regarding His saying ﴿ʿan sāq﴾ (from a shin) that it means "from a severity of the matter."

Ibn Qutaybah said: The origin of this is that when a man falls into a great matter that requires exertion in it, he hitches up his shin (shammara ʿan sāqihi). So uncovering the shin is borrowed for the place of hardship. He recited for Durayd ibn al-Simmah:

"Short of waistcloth, his shin half-bared, patient in the trial, a climber of the high ground."

He said: The interpretation of the verse is: the Day when the matter becomes severe, just as the matter in which one needs to hitch up his shin becomes severe.

Abu Ubaydah said: When the war or the matter becomes intense, it is said: "the matter uncovered its shin." The origin of it is that whoever falls into something requiring exertion hitches up his shin, so the shin and uncovering are borrowed for the place of hardship. Other lexicographers said the same, and the Arabs used this in their poetry. From that is the poet's saying:

"A brother of war, if war bites him, it bites him; and if war hitches up its shin, it hitches up."

And another's saying:

"The horses run at the time of sunrise, and war has stood up with us on a shin."

And another's saying as well:

"It has uncovered its shin, so tighten your belts; war has rushed upon you, so strive."

And another's saying also, about a year:

"It has uncovered its shin, red, stripping the flesh from its bones."

It was also said: the shin of a thing is its base and its support, like the shin of a tree and the shin of a man. That is: the Day the shin of the matter is uncovered, so its realities appear. It was said: the shin of Hell is uncovered. It was said: the shin of the Throne. It was said: it is an expression for nearness. It was said: the Lord, glorified is He, uncovers His light. What is the truth of this will come at the end of the discussion. And when the river of Allah comes, the river of Ma'qil is nullified.

The majority read yakshifu with the ya' (third person), in the passive voice. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas and Ibn Abi Ablah read takshifu with the ta' (feminine), in the active voice, meaning: the severity or the Hour. It was also read with the ta' in the passive, with the nun, and with the ta' damma and the kasra of the shin from uksifa al-amr, meaning: it entered into uncovering.

﴿And they are called to prostration, but they will not be able.﴾ al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: all of creation will prostrate to Allah in one prostration, and the disbelievers and hypocrites will remain wanting to prostrate but unable, because their spines will stiffen so they do not bend for prostration.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The veil is removed, so those who believed in Allah in the world fall down before Him in prostration, and the others are called to prostration but cannot, because they did not believe in Allah in the world.

The accusative of ﴿with their eyes humbled﴾ is a state (hal) from the pronoun in "yud'awna," and "their eyes" is raised by it as the subject. The attribution of humility to the eyes is because its effect appears in them, and it means submission and abasement. ﴿Humiliation will cover them﴾ meaning: severe humiliation, regret and remorse will overwhelm them. ﴿And they had been called to prostration﴾ in the world ﴿while they were sound﴾ meaning: safe from illnesses (p-١٥٢١), able to perform the act.

Ibrahim al-Taymi said: They are called with the adhan and the iqamah, but they refuse.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They hear "Hasten to success" but do not respond.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: By Allah, this verse was only revealed about those who stay away from the congregations.

It was also said: they are called by the obligation directed at them by the Law, but they do not respond. The clause ﴿while they were sound﴾ is in the place of an accusative as a state from the pronoun in "yud'un."

﴿So leave Me with whoever denies this statement.﴾ That is: leave Me to deal with him and entrust his affair to Me, for I will suffice you against him.

al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is: let not your heart be occupied with him; entrust him to Me, and I will suffice you in his matter.

The fa' is for the sequence of what follows from what precedes. "Man" is in the accusative by coordination with the pronoun of the speaker, or as an object with (maʿa). The intended "this statement" is the Qur'an, as said by al-Suddi. It was also said: it is the Day of Resurrection. In this is consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The clause ﴿We will draw them on gradually from where they do not know﴾ is a new sentence explaining the manner of their punishment, which is understood from His saying ﴿leave Me with whoever denies this statement﴾. The pronoun refers to "man" according to its meaning. The meaning: We will seize them with punishment while they are heedless, and drive them toward it degree by degree until We bring them into it from where they do not know, that this is istidraj (gradual enticement), because they think it is favor and do not reflect on its outcome or what they will meet at its end.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: He showers them with blessings and makes them forget gratitude.

al-Hasan said: How many are gradually enticed by kindness shown to them, how many are tested by praise directed at them, and how many are deceived by being covered over.

Istidraj is leaving hastening, and its origin is transfer from one state to another. It is said: istadraja fulan fulanan, meaning he extracted what was with him little by little. It is said: darrajahu ila kadha wa-istadrajahu, meaning he brought him near to gradualness, so he became gradual himself.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned that He gives respite to the wrongdoers, and said: ﴿And I give them respite﴾ meaning: I give them time so that they may increase in sin. The explanation of this has already passed in surah al-A'raf and al-Tur. The root of al-mala' is a period of time from the age; it is said: Allah gave him respite (amla Allahu lahu), meaning: He lengthened his term for him. Al-mala' with a short alif means wide land, named so for its extension. ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾ meaning: strong and severe, so nothing escapes Me. He, glorified is He, called His kindness a plan, just as He called it istidraj, because it takes the form of a plan with regard to its end, and described it as firm for the strength of its effect in causing destruction.

﴿Or do you ask them for payment?﴾ He, glorified is He, returned the speech to what preceded from His saying: ﴿Or do they have partners?﴾ meaning: or do you seek from them a reward for what you call them to of faith in Allah? ﴿So they are burdened with debt﴾ al-maghram is the indebtedness, meaning: they are burdened with the cost of that reward, and "burdened" means its carrying weighs heavily on them because of their stinginess in giving wealth, so they turned away from answering you for this reason. The interrogative is for rebuke and reproach to them. The meaning: you did not ask them for that, nor did you request it from them.

﴿Or do they have the unseen, so they write it down?﴾ That is: the Preserved Tablet, or everything hidden from them. So from that unseen they write what they want of arguments which they claim support their saying, and they dispute with you by what they write of that, and they judge for themselves what they wish, and thereby they consider themselves free from answering you and complying with what you say.

﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾ meaning: for His decree which He decreed in His prior knowledge. It was said: the judgment here is their being given respite and the delay of the victory of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over them. It was said: it is what He decreed upon him of conveying the message. It was said: this has been abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword (naskh: abrogation of one ruling by a later one). ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾ meaning Yunus, peace be upon him: do not be like him in anger, impatience and haste. The adverbial phrase in His saying ﴿when he called out﴾ is in the accusative governed by an implied genitive noun, meaning: your state should not be like his state at the time of his calling out. The clause ﴿while he was suppressed﴾ is in the place of an accusative as a state from the subject of "called out." Al-makzum means the one filled with rage and distress.

Qatadah said: Allah consoles His Prophet (ﷺ), commands him to be patient, and not to hasten as the companion of the fish hastened. Its story has already been explained in surah al-Anbiya', Yunus and al-Saffat. The calling out from him was with His saying: ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87]. It was also said: al-makzum is the one seized by his suppression, which is the passage of breath. This is what al-Mubarrad said. It was also said: it is the one held back. The first is more appropriate. From it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"And you, from love of Mayy, conceal sorrow, afflicted in heart, wounded in the heart, suppressed."

﴿Had a favor from his Lord not reached him﴾ meaning: had a favor from Allah not reached the companion of the fish, which is His granting him repentance, so that Allah accepted his repentance. ﴿He would have been cast out onto the barren land﴾ meaning: he would have been thrown out of the belly of the fish onto the face of the earth devoid of vegetation. ﴿And he would have been blameworthy﴾ meaning: he would be blamed and reproached for the sin he committed and be driven away from mercy. The clause is in the place of an accusative as a state from the pronoun in "nubidha."

al-Dahhak said: The favor here is prophethood.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It is his former worship.

Ibn Zayd said: it is his calling out with the words: ﴿There is no deity except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers.﴾ It was also said: he was blameworthy and removed (from mercy). It was also said: he was a sinner.

The majority of reciters read ﴿تَدارَكَهُ﴾ (*tadarakahu*, "overtook him") in the past tense. Al-Hasan, Ibn Humruz and al-A'mash read it with a shaddah on the dal, *tadarrakahu*. The original form is *tatadarakuhu*, a present tense verb with two taʾs, and one of them was assimilated into the following dal (*idghām*). This reading presents the past situation as if it were being narrated in the present. Ubayy, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas read *tadarakat-hu* with the feminine taʾ (تَدارَكَتْهُ), the feminine ending being attached to the verb because the subject is a feminine noun meaning "grace" or "mercy" (*niʿmah*, implied).

﴿So his Lord chose him﴾, meaning He selected him, chose him and preferred him for prophethood. ﴿And made him among the righteous﴾, meaning among those perfect in righteousness, and protected him from sin. It was also said: He restored prophethood to him, granted him intercession for himself and for his people, and sent him to a hundred thousand or more, as has been mentioned earlier.

﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve almost make you slip with their eyes﴾. The word "in" (*in*, إنْ) here is the lightened form of the heavy *inna*.

The majority of reciters read ﴿لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾ (*layuzliqunaka*) with a dammah on the yaʾ, from *azlaqahu*, meaning he caused his foot to slip; one says *azlaqahu ʿan mawdiʿihi* when one moves him from his place. Nafiʿ and the people of Madinah read it with a fathah on the yaʾ, from *zalaqa ʿan mawdiʿihi*, meaning he slipped or moved away from his place.

Al-Harawi said: that is, they will destroy you with their eyes, so they will make you slip from your station, in which Allah established you, out of enmity toward you. Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash, Mujahid and Abu Wa'il read ﴿لَيُرْهِقُونَكَ﴾ (*layurhiquna-ka*), meaning they will destroy you.

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿yuzliqunaka﴾ means they will turn you away from what you are upon, namely conveying the message. Al-Suddi and Saʿid ibn Jubayr also said the same.

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl and al-Akhfash said: they will tempt you (*yaftinunaka*).

Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: they will kill you (*layaqtulunaka*).

Al-Zajjaj said: the view of the linguists on this verse is that, out of the intensity of their hatred and enmity, they nearly bring you down with their gaze, a gaze of hatred. This is a common expression in speech; a speaker says, "He looked at me with a look that almost knocked me down," and "a look that almost devoured me."

Ibn Qutaybah said: Allah does not mean that they will harm you with their eyes as the one who casts the evil eye harms what he admires with his eye. Rather, He means that when you recite the Qur'an they look at you with a fierce gaze full of enmity and hatred, which almost brings you down, as the poet said:

*They contend with one another when they meet in an assembly,*
*with a gaze that removes the footprints of feet.*

﴿When they hear the Reminder﴾, meaning at the time they hear the Qur'an, out of their extreme dislike for it. The word "when" (*lamma*, لَمّا) is a temporal particle in the accusative, governed by ﴿يُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾. It was also said that it is a particle whose response (*jawab*) is omitted, because what precedes it indicates it; the meaning is: when they heard the Reminder, they almost made you slip. ﴿And they say, indeed he is mad﴾, meaning they attribute madness to him when they hear him reciting the Qur'an.

Allah responded to them by saying: ﴿And it is not but a reminder to the worlds.﴾ This sentence is independent, or it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (*ḥal*) from the subject of ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ (*yaqulun*, "they say"), meaning: while it is a reminder and a clarification of everything they need, or an honor for them, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44]. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), meaning that he is a reminder to the worlds or an honor for them.

Al-Bukhari and others narrated from Abu Saʿid, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Our Lord will uncover His shin, and every believing man and woman will prostrate to Him. Those who used to prostrate in the world for show and reputation will remain, and they will try to prostrate, but their backs will become one solid piece." This hadith is established through several chains in the two Sahihs and others. It has wordings, some of which are long, and it is a well-known, widely transmitted hadith.

Ibn Mandah narrated from Abu Hurayrah concerning the verse, he said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will uncover His shin.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mandah narrated from Ibn Mas'ud concerning the verse, he said: He will uncover His shin, blessed and exalted.

Abu Yaʿla, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat* (who declared it weak), and Ibn ʿAsakir narrated from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the verse, he said: "From a great light, so they will fall down prostrate before Him."

al-Firyabi, Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Mandah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning the verse, he said: "It will be uncovered from a great matter." Then he said: "The war has stood upon a shin."

He said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "He will uncover His shin, and every believer will prostrate, while the back of the disbeliever will become stiff and turn into one solid bone."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat* narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he was asked about the saying of Allah: ﴿The Day when a shin is uncovered﴾. He said: "If something of the Qur'an is obscure to you, seek it in poetry, for it is the register of the Arabs. Have you not heard the saying of the poet:"

*And the war stood with us upon a shin.*

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "This is a day of severe distress." Similar to this has been narrated from him through other chains. Allah, glory be to Him, has sufficed us in explaining this verse with what is authentically established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as you know. That does not imply anthropomorphism or likening Allah to creation, for ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾.

*They left every saying in favor of the saying of Muhammad,*
*so none believed in his religion like Mukhatir.*

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His saying: ﴿And they were being called to prostration while they were safe﴾. He said: "They are the disbelievers who were called in the world while they were secure, but today they are called while they are fearful."

al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shuʿab* narrated from him concerning the verse, he said: "A man hears the adhan but does not answer the prayer."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, concerning His saying: ﴿They would almost make you slip with their eyes﴾, he said: "They will pierce you with their eyes."

And another's saying also, about a year:

"It has uncovered its shin, red, stripping the flesh from its bones."

It was also said: the shin of a thing is its base and its support, like the shin of a tree and the shin of a man. That is: the Day the shin of the matter is uncovered, so its realities appear. It was said: the shin of Hell is uncovered. It was said: the shin of the Throne. It was said: it is an expression for nearness. It was said: the Lord, glorified is He, uncovers His light. What is the truth of this will come at the end of the discussion. And when the river of Allah comes, the river of Ma'qil is nullified.

The majority read yakshifu with the ya' (third person), in the passive voice. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas and Ibn Abi Ablah read takshifu with the ta' (feminine), in the active voice, meaning: the severity or the Hour. It was also read with the ta' in the passive, with the nun, and with the ta' damma and the kasra of the shin from uksifa al-amr, meaning: it entered into uncovering.

﴿And they are called to prostration, but they will not be able.﴾ al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: all of creation will prostrate to Allah in one prostration, and the disbelievers and hypocrites will remain wanting to prostrate but unable, because their spines will stiffen so they do not bend for prostration.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The veil is removed, so those who believed in Allah in the world fall down before Him in prostration, and the others are called to prostration but cannot, because they did not believe in Allah in the world.

The accusative of ﴿with their eyes humbled﴾ is a state (hal) from the pronoun in "yud'awna," and "their eyes" is raised by it as the subject. The attribution of humility to the eyes is because its effect appears in them, and it means submission and abasement. ﴿Humiliation will cover them﴾ meaning: severe humiliation, regret and remorse will overwhelm them. ﴿And they had been called to prostration﴾ in the world ﴿while they were sound﴾ meaning: safe from illnesses (p-١٥٢١), able to perform the act.

Ibrahim al-Taymi said: They are called with the adhan and the iqamah, but they refuse.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They hear "Hasten to success" but do not respond.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: By Allah, this verse was only revealed about those who stay away from the congregations.

It was also said: they are called by the obligation directed at them by the Law, but they do not respond. The clause ﴿while they were sound﴾ is in the place of an accusative as a state from the pronoun in "yud'un."

﴿So leave Me with whoever denies this statement.﴾ That is: leave Me to deal with him and entrust his affair to Me, for I will suffice you against him.

al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is: let not your heart be occupied with him; entrust him to Me, and I will suffice you in his matter.

The fa' is for the sequence of what follows from what precedes. "Man" is in the accusative by coordination with the pronoun of the speaker, or as an object with (maʿa). The intended "this statement" is the Qur'an, as said by al-Suddi. It was also said: it is the Day of Resurrection. In this is consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The clause ﴿We will draw them on gradually from where they do not know﴾ is a new sentence explaining the manner of their punishment, which is understood from His saying ﴿leave Me with whoever denies this statement﴾. The pronoun refers to "man" according to its meaning. The meaning: We will seize them with punishment while they are heedless, and drive them toward it degree by degree until We bring them into it from where they do not know, that this is istidraj (gradual enticement), because they think it is favor and do not reflect on its outcome or what they will meet at its end.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: He showers them with blessings and makes them forget gratitude.

al-Hasan said: How many are gradually enticed by kindness shown to them, how many are tested by praise directed at them, and how many are deceived by being covered over.

Istidraj is leaving hastening, and its origin is transfer from one state to another. It is said: istadraja fulan fulanan, meaning he extracted what was with him little by little. It is said: darrajahu ila kadha wa-istadrajahu, meaning he brought him near to gradualness, so he became gradual himself.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned that He gives respite to the wrongdoers, and said: ﴿And I give them respite﴾ meaning: I give them time so that they may increase in sin. The explanation of this has already passed in surah al-A'raf and al-Tur. The root of al-mala' is a period of time from the age; it is said: Allah gave him respite (amla Allahu lahu), meaning: He lengthened his term for him. Al-mala' with a short alif means wide land, named so for its extension. ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾ meaning: strong and severe, so nothing escapes Me. He, glorified is He, called His kindness a plan, just as He called it istidraj, because it takes the form of a plan with regard to its end, and described it as firm for the strength of its effect in causing destruction.

﴿Or do you ask them for payment?﴾ He, glorified is He, returned the speech to what preceded from His saying: ﴿Or do they have partners?﴾ meaning: or do you seek from them a reward for what you call them to of faith in Allah? ﴿So they are burdened with debt﴾ al-maghram is the indebtedness, meaning: they are burdened with the cost of that reward, and "burdened" means its carrying weighs heavily on them because of their stinginess in giving wealth, so they turned away from answering you for this reason. The interrogative is for rebuke and reproach to them. The meaning: you did not ask them for that, nor did you request it from them.

﴿Or do they have the unseen, so they write it down?﴾ That is: the Preserved Tablet, or everything hidden from them. So from that unseen they write what they want of arguments which they claim support their saying, and they dispute with you by what they write of that, and they judge for themselves what they wish, and thereby they consider themselves free from answering you and complying with what you say.

﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾ meaning: for His decree which He decreed in His prior knowledge. It was said: the judgment here is their being given respite and the delay of the victory of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over them. It was said: it is what He decreed upon him of conveying the message. It was said: this has been abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword (naskh: abrogation of one ruling by a later one). ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾ meaning Yunus, peace be upon him: do not be like him in anger, impatience and haste. The adverbial phrase in His saying ﴿when he called out﴾ is in the accusative governed by an implied genitive noun, meaning: your state should not be like his state at the time of his calling out. The clause ﴿while he was suppressed﴾ is in the place of an accusative as a state from the subject of "called out." Al-makzum means the one filled with rage and distress.

Qatadah said: Allah consoles His Prophet (ﷺ), commands him to be patient, and not to hasten as the companion of the fish hastened. Its story has already been explained in surah al-Anbiya', Yunus and al-Saffat. The calling out from him was with His saying: ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87]. It was also said: al-makzum is the one seized by his suppression, which is the passage of breath. This is what al-Mubarrad said. It was also said: it is the one held back. The first is more appropriate. From it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"And you, from love of Mayy, conceal sorrow, afflicted in heart, wounded in the heart, suppressed."

﴿Had a favor from his Lord not reached him﴾ meaning: had a favor from Allah not reached the companion of the fish, which is His granting him repentance, so that Allah accepted his repentance. ﴿He would have been cast out onto the barren land﴾ meaning: he would have been thrown out of the belly of the fish onto the face of the earth devoid of vegetation. ﴿And he would have been blameworthy﴾ meaning: he would be blamed and reproached for the sin he committed and be driven away from mercy. The clause is in the place of an accusative as a state from the pronoun in "nubidha."

al-Dahhak said: The favor here is prophethood.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It is his former worship.

Ibn Zayd said: it is his calling out with the words: ﴿There is no deity except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers.﴾ It was also said: he was blameworthy and removed (from mercy). It was also said: he was a sinner.

The majority of reciters read ﴿تَدارَكَهُ﴾ (*tadarakahu*, "overtook him") in the past tense. Al-Hasan, Ibn Humruz and al-A'mash read it with a shaddah on the dal, *tadarrakahu*. The original form is *tatadarakuhu*, a present tense verb with two taʾs, and one of them was assimilated into the following dal (*idghām*). This reading presents the past situation as if it were being narrated in the present. Ubayy, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas read *tadarakat-hu* with the feminine taʾ (تَدارَكَتْهُ), the feminine ending being attached to the verb because the subject is a feminine noun meaning "grace" or "mercy" (*niʿmah*, implied).

﴿So his Lord chose him﴾, meaning He selected him, chose him and preferred him for prophethood. ﴿And made him among the righteous﴾, meaning among those perfect in righteousness, and protected him from sin. It was also said: He restored prophethood to him, granted him intercession for himself and for his people, and sent him to a hundred thousand or more, as has been mentioned earlier.

﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve almost make you slip with their eyes﴾. The word "in" (*in*, إنْ) here is the lightened form of the heavy *inna*.

The majority of reciters read ﴿لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾ (*layuzliqunaka*) with a dammah on the yaʾ, from *azlaqahu*, meaning he caused his foot to slip; one says *azlaqahu ʿan mawdiʿihi* when one moves him from his place. Nafiʿ and the people of Madinah read it with a fathah on the yaʾ, from *zalaqa ʿan mawdiʿihi*, meaning he slipped or moved away from his place.

Al-Harawi said: that is, they will destroy you with their eyes, so they will make you slip from your station, in which Allah established you, out of enmity toward you. Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash, Mujahid and Abu Wa'il read ﴿لَيُرْهِقُونَكَ﴾ (*layurhiquna-ka*), meaning they will destroy you.

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿yuzliqunaka﴾ means they will turn you away from what you are upon, namely conveying the message. Al-Suddi and Saʿid ibn Jubayr also said the same.

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl and al-Akhfash said: they will tempt you (*yaftinunaka*).

Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: they will kill you (*layaqtulunaka*).

Al-Zajjaj said: the view of the linguists on this verse is that, out of the intensity of their hatred and enmity, they nearly bring you down with their gaze, a gaze of hatred. This is a common expression in speech; a speaker says, "He looked at me with a look that almost knocked me down," and "a look that almost devoured me."

Ibn Qutaybah said: Allah does not mean that they will harm you with their eyes as the one who casts the evil eye harms what he admires with his eye. Rather, He means that when you recite the Qur'an they look at you with a fierce gaze full of enmity and hatred, which almost brings you down, as the poet said:

*They contend with one another when they meet in an assembly,*
*with a gaze that removes the footprints of feet.*

﴿When they hear the Reminder﴾, meaning at the time they hear the Qur'an, out of their extreme dislike for it. The word "when" (*lamma*, لَمّا) is a temporal particle in the accusative, governed by ﴿يُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾. It was also said that it is a particle whose response (*jawab*) is omitted, because what precedes it indicates it; the meaning is: when they heard the Reminder, they almost made you slip. ﴿And they say, indeed he is mad﴾, meaning they attribute madness to him when they hear him reciting the Qur'an.

Allah responded to them by saying: ﴿And it is not but a reminder to the worlds.﴾ This sentence is independent, or it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (*ḥal*) from the subject of ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ (*yaqulun*, "they say"), meaning: while it is a reminder and a clarification of everything they need, or an honor for them, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44]. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), meaning that he is a reminder to the worlds or an honor for them.

Al-Bukhari and others narrated from Abu Saʿid, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Our Lord will uncover His shin, and every believing man and woman will prostrate to Him. Those who used to prostrate in the world for show and reputation will remain, and they will try to prostrate, but their backs will become one solid piece." This hadith is established through several chains in the two Sahihs and others. It has wordings, some of which are long, and it is a well-known, widely transmitted hadith.

Ibn Mandah narrated from Abu Hurayrah concerning the verse, he said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will uncover His shin.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mandah narrated from Ibn Mas'ud concerning the verse, he said: He will uncover His shin, blessed and exalted.

Abu Yaʿla, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat* (who declared it weak), and Ibn ʿAsakir narrated from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the verse, he said: "From a great light, so they will fall down prostrate before Him."

al-Firyabi, Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Mandah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning the verse, he said: "It will be uncovered from a great matter." Then he said: "The war has stood upon a shin."

He said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "He will uncover His shin, and every believer will prostrate, while the back of the disbeliever will become stiff and turn into one solid bone."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat* narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he was asked about the saying of Allah: ﴿The Day when a shin is uncovered﴾. He said: "If something of the Qur'an is obscure to you, seek it in poetry, for it is the register of the Arabs. Have you not heard the saying of the poet:"

*And the war stood with us upon a shin.*

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "This is a day of severe distress." Similar to this has been narrated from him through other chains. Allah, glory be to Him, has sufficed us in explaining this verse with what is authentically established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as you know. That does not imply anthropomorphism or likening Allah to creation, for ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾.

*They left every saying in favor of the saying of Muhammad,*
*so none believed in his religion like Mukhatir.*

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His saying: ﴿And they were being called to prostration while they were safe﴾. He said: "They are the disbelievers who were called in the world while they were secure, but today they are called while they are fearful."

al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shuʿab* narrated from him concerning the verse, he said: "A man hears the adhan but does not answer the prayer."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, concerning His saying: ﴿They would almost make you slip with their eyes﴾, he said: "They will pierce you with their eyes."

When He, glorified is He, finished mentioning the state of the disbelievers and comparing their trial to the trial of the people of the garden mentioned, He mentioned the state of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) and the good He has prepared for them.

He said: (p-١٥٢٠)﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing with their Lord are gardens of bliss.﴾ That is: for the God-fearing, who avoid what brings down His wrath, of disbelief and sins, with Him, mighty and majestic, in the Hereafter, are gardens of pure bliss, which is not mixed with turbidity and not spoiled by fear of its ending.

﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals?﴾ The interrogative is for denial (istinkar).

The chieftains of the disbelievers of Quraysh used to see their great share in this world and the small shares of the Muslims in it. When they heard the mention of the Hereafter and what Allah gives the Muslims in it, they said: "If what Muhammad claims is true, our state and theirs will be nothing but like their state in this world." So Allah, refuting them and rejecting their claim, said: ﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims...﴾ and the verse. The fa' here is for coordination (ataf) upon an implied clause, like its counterparts.

Then Allah rebuked them and said: ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ This crooked judgment, as if the matter of recompense were entrusted to you, so that you judge about it as you wish.

﴿Or do you have a scripture in which you study?﴾ That is: in which you read, and so you find the obedient equal to the disobedient. Similar to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do you have a clear authority? So bring your scripture.﴾ [al-Saffat: 156-157]. Then He, glorified is He, said: "Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose." The majority (al-Jumhur) read inna with a kasra, taking it as governed by tadrusun, meaning: you study in the Book.

﴿Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose.﴾ When the lam entered, the hamza was given a kasra, as in His saying: "I knew that you are indeed intelligent," with a kasra. Or it is by way of hikaya (quoting) of what is studied, as in His saying: ﴿And We left upon him among the later generations﴾ ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds﴾ [al-Saffat: 78-79]. It was said: the speech is complete at His saying: "you study," then He began: ﴿Indeed, for you therein is whatever you choose﴾, meaning: it is not for you to have that. Talhah ibn Musarrif and al-Dahhak read anna lakum with a fath on the hamza, taking the governing element to be tadrusun together with the addition of the emphatic lam. The meaning of takhayyarun is: you choose and desire.

Then He, glorified is He, increased the rebuke, and said: ﴿Or do you have oaths binding upon Us, extending to the Day of Resurrection?﴾ That is: firm, confirmed, utterly conclusive covenants. The meaning: Or do you have oaths upon Allah by which you secured that He would admit you into the Garden? His saying ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾ is connected to the implied element in lakum, meaning: they are established for you until the Day of Resurrection, and We are not released from their obligation until He judges you on that day. The answer to the oath is His saying: ﴿Indeed, for you is what you judge,﴾ because the meaning of ﴿Or do you have oaths﴾ is: or have We sworn to you?

Al-Razi said: The meaning is: Or have We guaranteed to you and sworn to you with emphatic oaths, utterly conclusive in affirmation?

It was also said: the speech is complete at His saying: ﴿to the Day of Resurrection,﴾ then He began: ﴿Indeed, for you is what you judge,﴾ meaning: the matter is not so.

The majority read bali'ah with a raf', as an attribute of aymān. al-Hasan and Zayd ibn Ali read it with a nasb, as a state (hal) of aymān, since it has been specified by the attribute, or of the pronoun in lakum, or of the pronoun in ʿalayna.

﴿Ask them, which of them stands surety for that?﴾ That is: ask them, O Muhammad, rebuking and reproaching them: which of them guarantees that judgment, which departs from what is right, that they will have in the Hereafter what the Muslims have there?

Ibn Kaysan said: al-Za'im here means the one who upholds the argument and the claim.

al-Hasan said: al-Za'im is the Messenger.

﴿Or do they have partners?﴾ who share with them in this statement, agreeing with them upon it. ﴿Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful﴾ in what they say. This is a command of incapacitation (taʿjiz), and the answer of the condition is omitted. It was also said: the meaning is: or do they have partners whom they make equal to the Muslims in the Hereafter?

﴿On the Day when the shin is uncovered﴾ "Yawm" is a time-adverb for His saying "let them bring," meaning: let them bring them on the Day when the shin is uncovered. It may also be an adverb governed by an implied verb, meaning: remember the Day when it is uncovered.

al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said regarding His saying ﴿ʿan sāq﴾ (from a shin) that it means "from a severity of the matter."

Ibn Qutaybah said: The origin of this is that when a man falls into a great matter that requires exertion in it, he hitches up his shin (shammara ʿan sāqihi). So uncovering the shin is borrowed for the place of hardship. He recited for Durayd ibn al-Simmah:

"Short of waistcloth, his shin half-bared, patient in the trial, a climber of the high ground."

He said: The interpretation of the verse is: the Day when the matter becomes severe, just as the matter in which one needs to hitch up his shin becomes severe.

Abu Ubaydah said: When the war or the matter becomes intense, it is said: "the matter uncovered its shin." The origin of it is that whoever falls into something requiring exertion hitches up his shin, so the shin and uncovering are borrowed for the place of hardship. Other lexicographers said the same, and the Arabs used this in their poetry. From that is the poet's saying:

"A brother of war, if war bites him, it bites him; and if war hitches up its shin, it hitches up."

And another's saying:

"The horses run at the time of sunrise, and war has stood up with us on a shin."

And another's saying as well:

"It has uncovered its shin, so tighten your belts; war has rushed upon you, so strive."

And another's saying also, about a year:

"It has uncovered its shin, red, stripping the flesh from its bones."

﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾ meaning: for His decree which He decreed in His prior knowledge. It was said: the judgment here is their being given respite and the delay of the victory of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over them. It was said: it is what He decreed upon him of conveying the message. It was said: this has been abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword (naskh: abrogation of one ruling by a later one). ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾ meaning Yunus, peace be upon him: do not be like him in anger, impatience and haste. The adverbial phrase in His saying ﴿when he called out﴾ is in the accusative governed by an implied genitive noun, meaning: your state should not be like his state at the time of his calling out. The clause ﴿while he was suppressed﴾ is in the place of an accusative as a state from the subject of "called out." Al-makzum means the one filled with rage and distress.

Qatadah said: Allah consoles His Prophet (ﷺ), commands him to be patient, and not to hasten as the companion of the fish hastened. Its story has already been explained in surah al-Anbiya', Yunus and al-Saffat. The calling out from him was with His saying: ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87]. It was also said: al-makzum is the one seized by his suppression, which is the passage of breath. This is what al-Mubarrad said. It was also said: it is the one held back. The first is more appropriate. From it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"And you, from love of Mayy, conceal sorrow, afflicted in heart, wounded in the heart, suppressed."

﴿Had a favor from his Lord not reached him﴾ meaning: had a favor from Allah not reached the companion of the fish, which is His granting him repentance, so that Allah accepted his repentance. ﴿He would have been cast out onto the barren land﴾ meaning: he would have been thrown out of the belly of the fish onto the face of the earth devoid of vegetation. ﴿And he would have been blameworthy﴾ meaning: he would be blamed and reproached for the sin he committed and be driven away from mercy. The clause is in the place of an accusative as a state from the pronoun in "nubidha."

al-Dahhak said: The favor here is prophethood.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It is his former worship.

Ibn Zayd said: it is his calling out with the words: ﴿There is no deity except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers.﴾ It was also said: he was blameworthy and removed (from mercy). It was also said: he was a sinner.

The majority of reciters read ﴿تَدارَكَهُ﴾ (*tadarakahu*, "overtook him") in the past tense. Al-Hasan, Ibn Humruz and al-A'mash read it with a shaddah on the dal, *tadarrakahu*. The original form is *tatadarakuhu*, a present tense verb with two taʾs, and one of them was assimilated into the following dal (*idghām*). This reading presents the past situation as if it were being narrated in the present. Ubayy, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas read *tadarakat-hu* with the feminine taʾ (تَدارَكَتْهُ), the feminine ending being attached to the verb because the subject is a feminine noun meaning "grace" or "mercy" (*niʿmah*, implied).

﴿So his Lord chose him﴾, meaning He selected him, chose him and preferred him for prophethood. ﴿And made him among the righteous﴾, meaning among those perfect in righteousness, and protected him from sin. It was also said: He restored prophethood to him, granted him intercession for himself and for his people, and sent him to a hundred thousand or more, as has been mentioned earlier.

﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve almost make you slip with their eyes﴾. The word "in" (*in*, إنْ) here is the lightened form of the heavy *inna*.

The majority of reciters read ﴿لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾ (*layuzliqunaka*) with a dammah on the yaʾ, from *azlaqahu*, meaning he caused his foot to slip; one says *azlaqahu ʿan mawdiʿihi* when one moves him from his place. Nafiʿ and the people of Madinah read it with a fathah on the yaʾ, from *zalaqa ʿan mawdiʿihi*, meaning he slipped or moved away from his place.

Al-Harawi said: that is, they will destroy you with their eyes, so they will make you slip from your station, in which Allah established you, out of enmity toward you. Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash, Mujahid and Abu Wa'il read ﴿لَيُرْهِقُونَكَ﴾ (*layurhiquna-ka*), meaning they will destroy you.

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿yuzliqunaka﴾ means they will turn you away from what you are upon, namely conveying the message. Al-Suddi and Saʿid ibn Jubayr also said the same.

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl and al-Akhfash said: they will tempt you (*yaftinunaka*).

Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: they will kill you (*layaqtulunaka*).

Al-Zajjaj said: the view of the linguists on this verse is that, out of the intensity of their hatred and enmity, they nearly bring you down with their gaze, a gaze of hatred. This is a common expression in speech; a speaker says, "He looked at me with a look that almost knocked me down," and "a look that almost devoured me."

Ibn Qutaybah said: Allah does not mean that they will harm you with their eyes as the one who casts the evil eye harms what he admires with his eye. Rather, He means that when you recite the Qur'an they look at you with a fierce gaze full of enmity and hatred, which almost brings you down, as the poet said:

*They contend with one another when they meet in an assembly,*
*with a gaze that removes the footprints of feet.*

﴿When they hear the Reminder﴾, meaning at the time they hear the Qur'an, out of their extreme dislike for it. The word "when" (*lamma*, لَمّا) is a temporal particle in the accusative, governed by ﴿يُزْلِقُونَكَ﴾. It was also said that it is a particle whose response (*jawab*) is omitted, because what precedes it indicates it; the meaning is: when they heard the Reminder, they almost made you slip. ﴿And they say, indeed he is mad﴾, meaning they attribute madness to him when they hear him reciting the Qur'an.

Allah responded to them by saying: ﴿And it is not but a reminder to the worlds.﴾ This sentence is independent, or it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (*ḥal*) from the subject of ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ (*yaqulun*, "they say"), meaning: while it is a reminder and a clarification of everything they need, or an honor for them, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44]. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), meaning that he is a reminder to the worlds or an honor for them.

Al-Bukhari and others narrated from Abu Saʿid, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Our Lord will uncover His shin, and every believing man and woman will prostrate to Him. Those who used to prostrate in the world for show and reputation will remain, and they will try to prostrate, but their backs will become one solid piece." This hadith is established through several chains in the two Sahihs and others. It has wordings, some of which are long, and it is a well-known, widely transmitted hadith.

Ibn Mandah narrated from Abu Hurayrah concerning the verse, he said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will uncover His shin.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mandah narrated from Ibn Mas'ud concerning the verse, he said: He will uncover His shin, blessed and exalted.

Abu Yaʿla, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat* (who declared it weak), and Ibn ʿAsakir narrated from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the verse, he said: "From a great light, so they will fall down prostrate before Him."

al-Firyabi, Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Mandah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning the verse, he said: "It will be uncovered from a great matter." Then he said: "The war has stood upon a shin."

He said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "He will uncover His shin, and every believer will prostrate, while the back of the disbeliever will become stiff and turn into one solid bone."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat* narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he was asked about the saying of Allah: ﴿The Day when a shin is uncovered﴾. He said: "If something of the Qur'an is obscure to you, seek it in poetry, for it is the register of the Arabs. Have you not heard the saying of the poet:"

*And the war stood with us upon a shin.*

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "This is a day of severe distress." Similar to this has been narrated from him through other chains. Allah, glory be to Him, has sufficed us in explaining this verse with what is authentically established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as you know. That does not imply anthropomorphism or likening Allah to creation, for ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾.

*They left every saying in favor of the saying of Muhammad,*
*so none believed in his religion like Mukhatir.*

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His saying: ﴿And they were being called to prostration while they were safe﴾. He said: "They are the disbelievers who were called in the world while they were secure, but today they are called while they are fearful."

al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shuʿab* narrated from him concerning the verse, he said: "A man hears the adhan but does not answer the prayer."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, concerning His saying: ﴿They would almost make you slip with their eyes﴾, he said: "They will pierce you with their eyes."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 69, verse 4–18 (part 1 of 2):

It is Meccan.
Al-Qurtubi said: this is the consensus (fi qawl al-jami').
Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "Surat al-Haqqah was revealed in Mecca."
Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr the like of this.
al-Tabarani narrated from Abu Barzah that "the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite al-Haqqah and its like in the dawn prayer."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: ﴿Al-Haqqah﴾ is the Resurrection, because the matter is established (yahiqqu) in it, and it is itself established (tahiqqu) beyond doubt.

al-Azhari said: it is said "haqaqtuhu fa-haqqaqtuhu uhiquhu," meaning: I contended with him and overcame him, I overcome him. So the Resurrection is "al-haqqah" because it confronts every disputant who contends against the religion of Allah with falsehood, and it overcomes every adversary.

In al-Sihah he said: "haqqahu" means he disputed with him over trivial matters; it is said, "He has no right (haqq) in it, nor contention (hiqaq), nor dispute (khusumah)." And al-tahaqqu means mutual disputing. Al-haqqah, al-haqqah and al-haqq are three dialects with the same meaning.

al-Wahidi said: it is the Resurrection according to the consensus of the exegetes, and it was named thus because it is the possessor of realities (dhat al-hawaqq) among matters; it is the true one that must be true, and all the rulings of the Resurrection are true and necessarily occur and exist.

al-Kisai and al-Mu'arrij said: al-haqqah is the Day of the Truth. It was also said: it was named thus because every person in it is deserving (haqiq) of being recompensed for his deeds. It was also said: it was named thus because it made obligatory (ahaqqat) the Fire for one people and the Garden for another people.

It is a subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is His saying: ﴿What is al-Haqqah?﴾, with "ma" interrogative being a second subject, and its predicate "al-Haqqah," and the sentence is a predicate for the first subject. The meaning: what is it in its state or its attributes? It was also said that the interrogative "ma" is a predicate for what follows it; and although this sentence is in the form of a question, its meaning is the magnification and glorification of its matter, as you say: "Zayd, what Zayd!" (p-1523) and we have already established this meaning in Surat al-Waqi'ah.

Then He, glorified is He, increased in magnifying its matter, enhancing its state and amplifying its terror, and said: ﴿And what will make you know what al-Haqqah is?﴾ That is: what has informed you what it is? That is, as if you do not know it when you have not witnessed it and seen the terrors that are in it, so it is as if it lies outside the circle of the knowledge of created beings.

Yahya ibn Salam said: I have been informed that everything in the Qur'an that says "and what will make you know" (wa ma adraka), He has made him know it and taught him; and everything about which He said "and what will make you know" (wa ma yudrika), He has informed him of it. "Ma" is a subject, and its predicate is "adraka"; and "ma al-haqqah" is a sentence of subject and predicate in a position of accusative by removal of the preposition, because adra takes a second object with the bi' as in His saying: ﴿nor would He have made you know of it﴾ [Yunus: 16]. So when the interrogative clause came to suspend it, it occupied the place of the second object. Without the hamzah it takes one object with bi', as in "daraytu bi-kadha"; and if it has the meaning of knowledge, it takes two objects. The sentence "wa ma adraka" is conjoined to the sentence "ma al-haqqah."

﴿Thamud and ʿAd denied the Striking Calamity﴾ That is, the Resurrection, and it was named thus because it strikes people with its terrors.

al-Mubarrad said: by al-qari'ah he meant the Qur'an which was sent down in the world upon their prophets, and they used to warn them with it and they denied them. It was also said: al-qari'ah is derived from al-qur'ah (lottery), because it raises some peoples and lowers others. The first is preferable, and the placing of "al-qari'ah" in the position of the pronoun of "al-haqqah" is to indicate the greatness of its terror and the frightfulness of its state; and the sentence is resumptive, explaining some of the states of al-Haqqah.

﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Overwhelming (al-taghiyah)﴾ Thamud are the people of Salih, whose account has been given before in more than one place, and the explanation of their dwellings and where they were. Al-taghiyah is the cry that exceeded its limit. It was also said: by their transgression and disbelief. The root of tughyan is exceeding the limit.

﴿And as for ʿAd, they were destroyed by a violent, icy wind﴾ ʿAd are the people of Hud, whose account has been given before, and the mention of their dwellings and where they were, in more than one place. Al-rih al-sarsar is the very cold wind, derived from al-sirr, which is cold. It was also said: it is the very loud one.

Mujahid said: the very hot poisonous winds (al-samum). And al-ʿatiyah is the one that rebelled against obedience, as if it rebelled against its keepers, so it did not obey them and they could not turn it back because of the severity of its blowing; or it rebelled against ʿAd, so they could not turn it back, rather it destroyed them.

﴿He subjected it against them for seven nights﴾ This sentence is resumptive, explaining the manner of their destruction. The meaning of "sakharaha" is: He gave it power over them; so said Muqatil. It was also said: He sent it.

al-Zajjaj said: He established it over them as He willed. Taskhir is the use of a thing with power. It is permissible that this sentence be an attribute of "rih," or a circumstance of it, either because it is specified by the attribute, or from the pronoun in "ʿatiyah." "And eight days" is conjoined to "seven nights." The accusative of "husuman" is by way of circumstance, meaning: possessing husum; or as a verbal noun with an implied verb, meaning: it cut them off (tahsimuhum husuman); or as an object. Al-husum is continuity; when a thing follows continuously without its beginning being cut off from its end, it is called husum.

al-Zajjaj said: what language requires in the meaning of His saying husuman is: it cuts them off, that is, it cuts them off completely, annihilates and destroys them.

al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: it cut them off, severed them and destroyed them.

al-Farra' said: al-husum is following one after another, from hasm al-da', which is cauterization, because its sufferer is cauterized with the cautery iron, and then that is followed upon him. From it is the saying of Abu Du'ad:
"Between them a long time separates them, continuing in it for years, husum."

al-Mubarrad said: it is from your saying "hasamtu al-shay'": when I cut it and separated it from other things. It was also said: al-hasm is uprooting. A sword is called husam because it cuts off the enemy from reaching his enmity. The meaning: it cut them off, that is, severed and removed them. From it is the saying of the poet:
"So it sent a barren east wind, and it turned upon them, and became husum."

Ibn Zayd said: that is, it cut them off, leaving none of them.
It is narrated from him that he said: it cut off the days and nights until it completed them, for it began at sunrise on the first day and ended at sunset on the last day.

al-Layth said: al-husum is ill omen, meaning it cuts off good from its people, like His saying ﴿in days of ill omen﴾ [Fussilat: 16].

It was disputed about its beginning: it was said: the morning of Sunday; it was said: the morning of Friday; it was said: the morning of Wednesday.

Wahb said: these are the days which the Arabs call "the days of the old woman" (ayyam al-ajuz); there was in them severe cold and a severe wind, and their beginning was Wednesday, and their end was Wednesday.

﴿So you see the people in it prostrate as if they were trunks of hollow palm trees﴾ The address is to everyone who is fit for it, on the assumption that had he been present at that time he would have seen that. The pronoun in "fiha" refers to the nights and days; it was also said: to the directions of the wind; the first is preferable.

Sara'a is the plural of sari', meaning dead. ﴿As if they were trunks of palm trees, hollowed out﴾ That is: fallen or decayed palm roots. It was also said: hollow, with no inside to them. The palm is masculine and feminine, and similar to it is His saying: ﴿as if they were trunks of uprooted palm trees﴾ [al-Qamar: 20], whose explanation has been given before, and it is a report of the enormity of their bodies.

Yahya ibn Salam said: He only said "hawiyah" because their bodies were emptied of their spirits, like hollow palm trees.

﴿So do you see any remnant of them?﴾ That is: of a remaining group, or of a remaining soul, or of a remainder, with "baqiyah" being a verbal noun like "al-ʿaqibah" and "al-ʿafiyah."

Ibn Jurayj said: they remained seven nights and eight days alive in the torment of the wind; when they reached evening on the eighth day they died, and the wind carried them and cast them into the sea.

﴿And Pharaoh came, and those before him﴾ That is: of the disbelieving nations.

The majority read "qablahu" with a fatha on the qaf and sukun on the ba', meaning: and those who preceded him of the past generations and the bygone nations. Abu ʿAmr and al-Kisai read it with a kasra on the qaf and fatha on the ba', meaning: and those who are on his side of his followers. Abu Hatim and Abu ʿUbayd preferred the second reading, for the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, Ubayy and those with him, and for the reading of Abu Musa "wa man yalqahu."

And "al-Mu'tafikat": the majority read "al-mu'tafikat" in the plural, and they are the towns of the people of Lut. al-Hasan and al-Jahdari read "al-mu'tafikah" in the singular, and the alif-lam is generic, so it is in the sense of the plural. The meaning: and the overturned ones came with the sin (al-khati'ah), that is, with the grave error or the sinful deed, taking it as a verbal noun.

The intended meaning is that they came with polytheism and sins.
Mujahid said: with sins; al-Jurjani said: with a great error.

﴿So they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord﴾ That is: every nation disobeyed its messenger sent to it.
al-Kalbi said: he was Musa; it was also said Lut, because he was nearer. It was said: "rasul" here means "risalah" (message), and of it is the saying of the poet:
"The slanderers have lied; I did not disclose to them a secret, nor did I send them with a message (rasul)."
That is, with a message.

﴿So He seized them with a seizing that was overwhelming﴾ That is: Allah seized them with a seizing that grew and exceeded the seizings of other nations. The meaning: it was extremely severe to the utmost degree. It is said: "raba al-shay'" (it grew) when it increased and multiplied.

al-Zajjaj said: it exceeds the other seizings. Mujahid said: severe.

﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed﴾ That is: it exceeded its limit in rising and height; and that was in the time of Nuh, when his people persisted in disbelief and denied him. It was also said: the water overflowed over its keepers from the angels, out of anger for its Lord, so they could not restrain it.

Qatadah said: it rose above everything by fifteen cubits.
﴿We carried you in the sailing ship﴾ That is: in the loins of your fathers; or We carried them and We carried you in their loins, giving precedence to the addressees over the absent ones.

Al-jariyah is the ship of Nuh, and it was named jariyah because it runs (tajri) on the water. The position of "fi al-jariyah" is accusative as a circumstance, meaning: We raised you above the water while you were in the ship.

Since the purpose of mentioning the stories of the nations and what befell them of punishment is to deter this community from following them in disobeying the Messenger, He said:
﴿That We might make it a reminder for you﴾ That is: that We might make these matters mentioned a lesson and an admonition for you, O community of Muhammad, by which you may derive proof of the great power of Allah and the wondrous perfection of His workmanship; or that We might make this deed, which is an expression of the saving of the believers and the drowning of the disbelievers, a reminder for you.
﴿And that a retaining ear may retain it﴾ That is: an ear that retains what it has heard, preserving it after hearing it.

al-Zajjaj said: it is said "awaytu kadha," meaning: I memorized it in myself, I memorize it with comprehension (wa'yan), and "wa'aytu al-ilm" and "wa'aytu ma qultahu kullahu" have the same meaning; and "awaytu al-mata'" means I put the goods into the container, and it is said of whatever you have put into something other than yourself "awaytahu" with an alif, and of what you have memorized in yourself "wa'aytahu" without an alif.

Qatadah said in explaining the verse: an ear that hears and understands what it hears.
al-Farra' said: the meaning is that every ear may retain it as an admonition for whoever comes after.

The majority read "ta'iyaha" with a kasra on the ʿayn.
Talhah ibn Musarrif, Humayd al-A'raj, and Abu ʿAmr in one narration from him read it with a sukun on the ʿayn, likening this word to "rahim" and "shahid," though it is not of that pattern.

al-Razi said: it is narrated from Ibn Kathir that he read with sukun on the ʿayn, making the imperfect prefix together with what follows it like one word, so he lightened it and made it sukun, as one makes the middle letter sukun in "fakhdh," "kabd," and "katf," end of quote. The better view is that this is from the category of treating the connection as the pause, as in the reading of one who read "wa ma yush'irkum" [al-An'am: 109] with sukun on the ra'. al-Qurtubi said: the reading differed concerning it from ʿAsim and Ibn Kathir, meaning ta'iyaha.

﴿Then when the Trumpet is blown with one blast﴾ This is the beginning of the explanation of al-Haqqah and how it occurs after the explanation of its matter through the destruction of the deniers.

ʿAtaʾ said: He means the first blast.
al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: He means the last blast.

The majority read "nafkhatun wahidatun" with raf' in both, on the basis that nafkhatun is raised as a deputy subject, and wahidatun is an emphasis for it; and the masculine verb is acceptable because of the separation.
Abu al-Simmak read them both in the accusative, on the basis that the deputy is the prepositional phrase.

al-Zajjaj said: His saying "fi al-sur" stands in the place of what has not named its agent.

﴿And the earth and the mountains are lifted up﴾ That is: they are raised from their places and uprooted from their settlements by divine power.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 69, verses 4–18 (part 2 of 2):

The majority (al-Jumhur) read "ḥumilat" with a light (unshaddated) mīm.

Al-A'mash, Ibn Abi 'Abla, Ibn Miqsam, and Ibn 'Amir in one narration from him read it with a doubled mīm (ḥummilat), either for intensification (li-l-takthīr) or for transitivity (li-l-ta'diya).

﴿Then they will be crushed with one crushing﴾, meaning they will be broken with one breaking, with no addition to it; or they will be struck with one blow, one against the other, until they become a heaped-up sand dune (kathīban mahīlan) and scattered dust (habā'an munbatthan).

Al-Farra' said: "He did not say 'fa-dukkakna' because He made the mountains all as one unit." A parallel is the Most High's saying: ﴿Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We separated them?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 30]. It has also been said: "dukkatā" means "spread out with one spreading," and from this comes indakka sanam al-ba'īr (the hump of the camel collapsed), when it spread out flat on its back.

﴿So on that Day the Inevitable Event will occur﴾, meaning the Resurrection will be established.

﴿And the sky will be split open, for it will be frail on that Day﴾, meaning it will split open by the descent of the angels within it, so on that Day it will be weak and loose.

Al-Zajjaj said: "Whatever has become extremely weak is called waahin (wāhin), since it has become frail (qad wahiya)." Al-Farra' said: "Wahyuha (its frailty) is its splitting apart."

﴿And the angels will be upon its borders﴾, meaning the angels as a class will be upon its edges and sides. Arjā' is the plural of raja (rajan), a defective noun whose dual is rajawān, like qafā and qafawān. The meaning is that when the sky splits open, and it is their dwelling, they will take refuge at its edges.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God commands the lowest heaven and it splits open, and the angels will be upon its rims until the Lord commands them, so they descend to the earth and encompass the earth and whoever is upon it.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The meaning is "and the angels will be upon the borders of the world," i.e., they will descend to the earth. It has also been said: when the sky becomes pieces, the angels will stand upon those pieces which are not themselves split.

﴿And the Throne of your Lord will be borne above them on that Day by eight﴾, meaning eight angels will bear it above their heads on the Day of Resurrection. It has also been said: eight rows of angels whose number none knows except God, the Mighty and Majestic. It has also been said: eight parts out of nine parts of the angels, as said by al-Kalbi and others.

﴿On that Day you will be presented﴾, meaning the servants will be presented before God for their reckoning. A similar verse is: ﴿And they will be presented before your Lord in rows﴾ [al-Kahf: 48]. That presentation before Him, glory be to Him, is not so that He may know by it what He did not already know.

Rather, it is a presentation of testing and rebuke concerning deeds. The clause ﴿no secret of yours will be hidden﴾ is in a position of accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the pronoun in "tu'raḍūn" (you will be presented), meaning: you will be presented in a state in which nothing of your essences, sayings, or deeds, whatever they are, is hidden from God, glory be to Him. The implied sense is: "any soul that is hidden, or any deed that is hidden."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Ḥātim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-Ḥāqqah is one of the names of the Resurrection."

al-Firyabi, 'Abd ibn Ḥumayd, and Ibn Jarir narrated from him, who said: God never sends any wind except by a measure, nor any drop of water except by a measure, except on the day of Noah and the day of 'Ad. As for the day of Noah, the water overflowed over its keepers, so they had no power over it; then he recited ﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed﴾. As for the day of 'Ad, the wind rebelled against its keepers, so they had no power over it; then he recited ﴿with a violent, roaring wind﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated similarly from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (p. 1525).

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "I was helped by the east wind (al-Ṣabā), and 'Ad were destroyed by the west wind (al-Dabūr)."

Ibn Abi Ḥātim narrated from Ibn 'Umar, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: The keepers over 'Ad were commanded only with an amount equal to the place of a ring from the wind; it rebelled against the keepers and came out from the sides of the doors. That is His saying: ﴿with a violent, roaring wind﴾. He said: its rebellion was that it rebelled against the keepers.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Ḥātim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿with a violent, roaring wind﴾: "al-ghālibah" (the overpowering).

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Manṣur, 'Abd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Ṭabarani, and al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it, narrated from Ibn Mas'ud concerning His saying ﴿ḥusūman﴾: "consecutive ones."

'Abd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarir narrated through several chains from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿ḥusūman﴾: "successive," and in another wording: "consecutive ones."

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him ﴿as if they were trunks of hollow palm trees﴾, saying: they are its roots; and concerning His saying ﴿hollow﴾, he said: ruined.

Sa'id ibn Manṣur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him also concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed﴾, he said: it overflowed over its keepers and descended, and no water descended from the sky except by measure or weight, except in the time of Noah, when it overflowed over its keepers and descended without measure or weight.

Sa'id ibn Manṣur, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Ḥilya narrated through the chain of Makhul "from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib concerning His saying ﴿and an attentive ear will retain it﴾, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to me: 'I asked God to make it your ear, O 'Ali.' 'Ali said: 'I have not heard anything from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and forgotten it.'" Ibn Kathir said: this is a mursal narration.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Ḥātim, al-Wahidi, Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn 'Asakir, and Ibn al-Najjar narrated from Buraydah, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to 'Ali: 'God commanded me to bring you near and not to push you away, and to teach you, and that you should retain, and it is right for you to retain.' So this verse was revealed: ﴿and an attentive ear will retain it﴾. You are the attentive ear, O 'Ali." Ibn Kathir said: it is not authentic.

'Abd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn 'Umar concerning His saying ﴿an attentive ear﴾: "an ear that understood from God."

al-Ḥākim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b concerning His saying ﴿And the earth and the mountains will be lifted and crushed with one crushing﴾, who said: they will become dust upon the faces of the disbelievers, not upon the faces of the believers, and that is His saying: ﴿Faces on that Day will be upon them dust, covered by darkness﴾ [Abasa: 40–41].

Ibn Abi Ḥātim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas ﴿So it will be on that Day frail﴾, who said: "split apart."

al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Ḥātim narrated from him concerning His saying ﴿and the angels will be upon its borders﴾, who said: "upon its rims, upon what has not collapsed from it."

'Abd ibn Ḥumayd, 'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi in his refutation of the Jahmiyya, Abu Ya'la, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Khuzaymah, al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Khatib in Talkhis al-Mutashabih narrated from him also concerning His saying ﴿and the Throne of your Lord will be borne above them on that Day by eight﴾, who said: "eight angels in the form of mountain goats (al-awʿāl)."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Ḥātim narrated from him also through several chains concerning the verse, who said: it is said: eight rows of angels whose number none knows except God; and it is said: eight angels whose heads are at the Throne in the seventh heaven and whose feet are in the lowest earth, and they have horns like the horns of a mountain goat, the distance from the root of one of their horns to its tip being five hundred years.

Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection three times. As for two presentations, there is disputation and excuses; as for the third, then the scrolls will fly into hands, so one will take his record in his right hand and another will take it in his left."

Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th narrated similarly from Ibn Mas'ud.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 69, verse 4–18 (part 1 of 2):

It is Meccan.
Al-Qurtubi said: this is the consensus (fi qawl al-jami').
Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "Surat al-Haqqah was revealed in Mecca."
Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr the like of this.
al-Tabarani narrated from Abu Barzah that "the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite al-Haqqah and its like in the dawn prayer."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: ﴿Al-Haqqah﴾ is the Resurrection, because the matter is established (yahiqqu) in it, and it is itself established (tahiqqu) beyond doubt.

al-Azhari said: it is said "haqaqtuhu fa-haqqaqtuhu uhiquhu," meaning: I contended with him and overcame him, I overcome him. So the Resurrection is "al-haqqah" because it confronts every disputant who contends against the religion of Allah with falsehood, and it overcomes every adversary.

In al-Sihah he said: "haqqahu" means he disputed with him over trivial matters; it is said, "He has no right (haqq) in it, nor contention (hiqaq), nor dispute (khusumah)." And al-tahaqqu means mutual disputing. Al-haqqah, al-haqqah and al-haqq are three dialects with the same meaning.

al-Wahidi said: it is the Resurrection according to the consensus of the exegetes, and it was named thus because it is the possessor of realities (dhat al-hawaqq) among matters; it is the true one that must be true, and all the rulings of the Resurrection are true and necessarily occur and exist.

al-Kisai and al-Mu'arrij said: al-haqqah is the Day of the Truth. It was also said: it was named thus because every person in it is deserving (haqiq) of being recompensed for his deeds. It was also said: it was named thus because it made obligatory (ahaqqat) the Fire for one people and the Garden for another people.

It is a subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is His saying: ﴿What is al-Haqqah?﴾, with "ma" interrogative being a second subject, and its predicate "al-Haqqah," and the sentence is a predicate for the first subject. The meaning: what is it in its state or its attributes? It was also said that the interrogative "ma" is a predicate for what follows it; and although this sentence is in the form of a question, its meaning is the magnification and glorification of its matter, as you say: "Zayd, what Zayd!" (p-1523) and we have already established this meaning in Surat al-Waqi'ah.

Then He, glorified is He, increased in magnifying its matter, enhancing its state and amplifying its terror, and said: ﴿And what will make you know what al-Haqqah is?﴾ That is: what has informed you what it is? That is, as if you do not know it when you have not witnessed it and seen the terrors that are in it, so it is as if it lies outside the circle of the knowledge of created beings.
